chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sama'a ibn Mehran from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him.

He said: When a worshiper's sins have increased and he does not find anything to atone for them, God, Mighty and Majestic, afflicts him with grief in this world to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He ails his body to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He intensifies his death to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He punishes him in his grave so that he may meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day he meets Him with nothing testifying against him for any of his sins.

key_terms.أَسْقَمَ بَدَنَهُ: He ails his body; physical illness as a means of spiritual purification
key_terms.الْحُزْنِ: Grief; sadness and sorrow sent as a divine trial
key_terms.ذُنُوبُهُ: His sins; the accumulated transgressions of the servant
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: His grave; the intermediate realm (barzakh) where punishment may occur
key_terms.يُكَفِّرُهَا: To atone them; the process of expiating sins through suffering

ai.seo_question: How does God purify a believer's sins through worldly suffering according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes a progressive divine mercy through which God purifies a sinful believer before the Day of Judgment. When a person's sins accumulate beyond what their good deeds can atone, God sends four escalating trials -- grief, bodily illness, a difficult death, and punishment in the grave -- each designed to expiate sins so that the person may ultimately meet God free of any testimony against them. This teaching was given to comfort believers who endure worldly hardships, reframing suffering as God's compassionate intervention to ensure their salvation.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham b. Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Sama`a b. Mehran from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as).

He said: When a worshiper’s sins have increased, and he does not find anything to atone them by, Allah afflicts him with grief in this world to atone him of them. Then, his body will ail him so that it may atone him of them. Then, his death will be intensified for him so that it may atone him of them. Then, he will be punished in the grave so that he may meet Allah on the Day that he meets Him without anything of his sins testifying against him.
